status: complete: 83 cases, run with `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (83 pass as tests; verdicts 76 pass, 7 unclear, 0 fail)
summary: Of 83 black-box cases on the guard's state, 76 pass, 7 are unclear and none fail: the double-send, concurrency, restart (20 SIGKILL points) and latch batteries pass as §11 states them, as do D13 and D14 at guard level, outcomes, windows, attempts, redeem, tampering, the lock and replay. The unclear cases are gaps the spec leaves undecided, the sharpest being that restore and replay() accept a sealed release entry whose signature is all zeros (S83), that an attempt still able to land stops counting once its admission leaves a short window (S82), and that a receipt reported expired still redeems (S36). Restore also trusts a re-sealed reservation that replay() would reject (S68), a release's expiry is judged on the caller's stepped-back 'at' (S80), and an unreadable lock file refuses to start with an 'undefined' message (S81).

spec_questions: S35: redeem() with no block height for a receipt that has an expiry. The guard refuses (fail-closed). §3 does not say; should the spec state it, since guardedSigner's rpc is optional?

S36: should redeem() refuse a receipt whose attempt was reported expired (or failed)? Today a receipt reported expired, whose value and fees were released and whose intent admits attempt 2, still redeems ok while within its height, so both attempts could be signed and land. §8 reports expired precisely when 'its bytes were never signed, so they cannot land'; the receipt should then be spent, or redeem should check the outcome.

S77: the D14 hold is measured from the intent's first attempt. With maxAttempts > 1, an attempt admitted late in the window (here 10 s before) is released as soon as the window since the first attempt passes, though, being unreported, it may have landed. Is 'first attempt' intended, rather than 'latest unresolved attempt'? The window cap still counts it, which bounds the cost.

S80: which clock judges a release's expiry? Windows run on the latest recorded time (§7), but release(text, sig, at) judges 'expires' against the 'at' passed, so an operator release that has expired by the record's own clock is accepted on a stepped-back 'at'. The operator's expiry is then only as strong as the caller's clock.

S81: a lock file that names no process (empty or unparsable, e.g. a crash between creating and writing it) refuses to start, as does one naming another host. Both are fail-safe; should the spec say so, and how an operator clears it? The refusal message reads 'locked by process undefined on undefined'.

S68: does 'on start, the guard verifies the chain and replays it' mean restore recomputes each decision (as replay() does), or only re-applies recorded entries? Today a re-sealed last entry with a lowered reservation restores, and frees cap; replay() of the same record catches it on 'amounts'. Running the decision check at start would close the gap at the cost of start time. (A writer of the file is outside SDK mode's trust, §2.1; the Alpha's anchor covers wholesale rewrites, not a re-sealed head.)

S82: is an attempt that can still land counted against the window only by its admission time? With windowMs shorter than a blockhash's life (~150 blocks), an attempt still in flight leaves the window, the guard holds its intent but admits other payments against the freed cap, and both can land inside one window. §7's 'Meanwhile the window caps count the attempt' reads as if a held attempt stays counted. Either keep held attempts counted, or require windowMs to exceed the blockhash lifetime (rule 0).

S83: should restore and replay() verify a recorded release's ed25519 signature against latch.releaseKey? Today a sealed release entry with an all-zero signature un-latches the guard on restore, and replay() reports the record sound. The signature is kept in ReleaseV1, so both can check it; replay() in particular is what an auditor runs.
own_mistakes_fixed: S78: the first version used bytes [0xde, 0xad, i] as a malformed message; 0xde has its high bit set, so the guard rightly read it as a version byte and denied unsupported-version (rule 2). Changed to [1, 2, i] (legacy, too short): malformed-proposal.

S69: the first version killed the child at a random 0-1500 ms after its first ack; the stream finished in ~460 ms on that disk, so 13 of 20 kills landed after it was done. Narrowed to 0-420 ms and added an assertion that at least 18 of 20 kills land mid-stream. On the new folder's slower disk (~1 entry/ms) that range reached only the first 400 of 3000 entries, so the kill point is now a count of acks read (1, then random to 2900), which spreads over the stream on any disk.
S51: an edit while extending it inserted `arguments[0]` inside an async arrow function; rewritten to take the first decision from sixEntries() before it ran.
Runner: Node 26 resolves `node --test tests/` as a module path and fails; the suite runs as `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`.
